sentences.text:
This writ petition has been filed for the following reliefs: -
"for issuance of an appropriate writ, order, direction for quashing the order dated 19th December, 2003 as contained in letter No. 278 passed under the signature of the General Manager, Kathara Colliery, whereby and where under the claim of the petitioner for payment of compensation at prevalent market rate and to provide employment to the petitioners in lieu of the fact that the land have been acquired by the respondents and for further direction upon the respondents to grant employment to the petitioners under the Policy of granting employment to Displaced persons or land oustees and to pay to the petitioners compensation for the land acquired being 6.31 acres at the prevailing market rate and asking them to make fresh calculation on the said basis.
And/or For the issuance of any other appropriate writ/order/direction for doing conscionable justice to the petitioners."

3. Learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted that three employments have been provided,
but compensation has not been paid with regard to acquisition of land.
The concerned notification for acquisition of land is of the year 1965 and the acquisition was under the provisions of Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition and Development) Act, 1957.

entities.text: Coal Bearing Areas (Acquisition and Development) Act, 1957
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
4. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondents has submitted that at one point of time,
the tribunal under the aforesaid Act was non- functional as per the earlier counter affidavit, but they have filed an affidavit stating that the tribunal is functional.

She submits that the petitioners have remedy under the provisions of Section 14 of the aforesaid Act, 1957 and such claim of the petitioners may not be adjudicated under writ jurisdiction which are disputed claims.
She also submits that it may be observed that all the contentions of the parties be kept open.

5. Considering the aforesaid submissions and the fact that there are disputed questions of facts involved in the present case which cannot be adjudicated under writ jurisdiction, this Court is not inclined to proceed any further in this writ petition.
6. Accordingly, this writ petition is disposed of enabling the petitioners to approach the concerned tribunal constituted under the provisions of the aforesaid Act, 1957.
7. All the contentions of the parties are kept open.

8. Considering the fact that the matter has remained pending before this Court since 2004 and the acquisition being an old one, it is expected that the tribunal will take appropriate steps for expeditious disposal of the matter.
9. Pending interlocutory application, if any, is closed.

(Anubha Rawat Choudhary, J.) Mukul M/D Muslim Ansari vs M/S Central Coalfields Ltd on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88065463/
